title: Raga Jaitsri
hookLine: Jaitsri opens with a hand placed on a forehead

lines: A FEVER AT THREE IN THE MORNING.
A COOL HAND ON THE FOREHEAD.
cards: Someone slips into a dark room at three in the morning, sits on the edge of a feverish child's bed, and lays a cool hand on the child's forehead. Nothing gets fixed. The fever is still there.
But the room changes. That kind of strength doesn't shout. It arrives, it stays, and it steadies.
Today's raga opens its pages with a hand like that. Today: Raga Jaitsri, which tradition links with longing and quiet strength.

teach.b: Jaitsri comes after Dhanasri in the Granth's order. Its first hymn is by Guru Ram Das, mahala four, and it begins with two pictures.

teach.h: THE JEWEL OF THE NAME IN THE HEART.
teach.b: In paraphrase: the jewel of the Name has come to dwell in my heart; the Guru has placed his hand on my forehead. The jewel is inside, hidden, precious, not for show.

teach.h: A HAND PLACED ON THE FOREHEAD.
teach.b: The hand is outside, a familiar gesture of blessing: an elder's palm resting on a younger head. A touch from outside, a treasure within. Now the longing.

A raga of longing usually sounds like reaching for something far away. But this hymn starts from what has already been given. Its longing is to stay near the one who gave it, to keep feeling that hand.

Strength and longing turn out to be one movement seen from two sides: you lean toward what steadies you. The hymn doesn't say the hard things vanished. It says something precious now lives inside, put there by a touch.
Not the strength of a wall, which keeps everything out, but of a keel under a boat, unseen, keeping it upright in the wind. Jaitsri's opening pages are calm, and the calm has weight.

how: Shabads from the Jaitsri section of the Guru Granth Sahib are sung in Raga Jaitsri in kirtan, and Guru Ram Das's opening hymn, about the jewel of the Name and the Guru's hand on the forehead, is one of them.

o: the raga after Dhanasri, linked with quiet strength
the raga of morning, opened by a plea of need
a hymn sung while a child is being blessed

games.q: what's inside the raga — tap the pairs.
p: the Name, dwelling in the heart

s: Jaitsri's first hymn says the hard things vanished
it says the jewel of the Name now dwells in the heart; it makes no promise that trouble disappears.
Jaitsri's opening hymn is by Guru Ram Das
mahala four, with the jewel in the heart and the Guru's hand on the forehead.

games.q: the hymn says something precious now lives in the heart. how did it get there?
o: the Guru placed his hand on the forehead.
games.why: in Guru Ram Das's hymn the change comes with a touch: the Guru's hand on the forehead, and the jewel of the Name in the heart.

practice: If it feels right, rest your own palm lightly on your forehead for a few breaths and feel its weight and warmth, then let it fall to your lap and see whether the steadiness stays.
Bring to mind someone whose presence has steadied you without a word, and stay with them a while, saying Waheguru softly if you pray, or simply remembering them if you don't.
